learning_outcomes.text: The course provides students with the basic knowledge and methodological tools necessary to analyze the main problems of measurement theory. These tools can enable the student to grasp the causal connections between physical phenomena in the empirical world and the properties of physical quantities in the symbolic world, together with the main characteristics that an adequate measurement method aimed at these properties must present, and to understand the implications of measurement choices on the final outcomes of the measurement.

The course provides skills and tools necessary to apply knowledge in practice, fostering the ability to use basic methodological tools to define, design, and implement an adequate metrological approach to address ordinary measurement problems in typical engineering applications in the information sector.

syllabus_topics: Theoretical foundations of measurement: concept of measure and measurement
Expression and representation of a measurement result
Main metrological characteristics of measuring instruments
Main measurement methodologies and procedures for signal analysis in the time domain (direct frequency measurement, direct period measurement, time interval measurement, phase difference measurement)
Main measurement methodologies and procedures for signal analysis in the amplitude domain (measurement of DC voltages, measurement of AC voltages)
Architecture and modes of use of basic instrumentation for signal analysis in the amplitude domain (digital voltmeters and multimeters)
Architecture and modes of use of basic instrumentation for signal analysis in the time domain (digital counters, digital oscilloscopes)
Problems of instrument insertion into measurement circuits and connection between different equipment
institution: Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica (L-8, Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione)
